items.summary: Finish the Shell authority purge so the Shell becomes projection/input only and stops acting like a shadow runtime.

items.summary: Remove the remaining Alpine boot/runtime dependency once the retirement guard is green.

items.summary: Implement end-to-end unified trace_id propagation from initial request through Orchestration, workflows, tools, Kernel receipts, Sentinel, and final response.

items.summary: Assimilation and longer-horizon runtime work can stay parked here until the red and yellow closure work is materially better.

items.title: Keep lower-pressure valid backlog items parked
items.summary: These are still valid backlog items, but they are not the current forcing function.

items.title: Keep Layer 3 and OS-readiness work parked behind current closure work
items.source_family: OS-Readiness Wave - Layer 3 to True OS Migration
items.summary: Layer 3 and OS-readiness work remains important, but it should stay behind the current Shell, workflow, and trace closure push.

items.title: Keep Tauri migration strategically queued
items.source_family: Tauri Desktop App Migration + Memory Fix Wave
items.summary: Tauri migration remains strategically valuable, but it should not outrun the deeper architecture cleanup already underway.

items.title: Remove unused Rust imports in narrow batches
items.summary: No unused-import warnings were observed before cargo check stopped on the outside-lane dashboard compat unclosed delimiter. This item is blocked until that compile blocker clears and a complete warning surface can be captured.

items.title: Delete dead combined artifacts in safe batches
items.summary: Deletion candidates exist in the combined artifact classification, but deletion is blocked until the outside-lane dashboard compat compile blocker is fixed so domain batches can be validated.

items.title: Decompose live combined artifact debt
items.summary: Live split-debt artifacts are classified, but decomposition is blocked until the outside-lane dashboard compat compile blocker is fixed so owner-scoped renames can be validated.

items.title: Define the shared AgentRuntimeTurnEnvelope contract
items.summary: Create the engine-agnostic context envelope contract so native Infring, Codex, Claude Code, Grok Code, and socket engines receive the same bounded conversation, memory, permission, artifact, and tool-grant shape.
items.progress_note: In progress: added AgentRuntimeContextPack and context authority boundary contracts. Remaining: decide whether to preserve the AgentRuntimeTurnEnvelope name as wrapper around the pack or retire that wording in favor of the pack contract.

items.title: Build Gateway-owned runtime context assembly
items.summary: Have Gateway assemble bounded conversation windows, summaries, refs, session identity, and context budgets for every runtime turn instead of passing only the latest prompt.
items.progress_note: In progress: Gateway now assembles bounded context projections, persists transitional rows, prefers the Kernel materializer bridge, and falls back only when Kernel materializer is unavailable. Remaining: package Kernel materializer binary for production runtime so fallback becomes rare.

items.title: Bridge unified memory into runtime context
items.summary: Attach bounded relevant memory projections and refs to the runtime envelope so engine switches preserve durable Infring context without exposing raw memory dumps.
items.progress_note: In progress: Layer-2 context topology now carries bounded text previews through Kernel materialization. Remaining: retrieve relevant durable unified-memory projections by scope, not only session/conversation atoms.

items.title: Inject shared context into CLI and socket adapters
items.summary: Render the shared envelope into a consistent bounded adapter preamble for Codex, Claude Code, Grok Code, custom socket engines, and native Infring without engine-specific prompt drift.
items.progress_note: In progress: Codex, Claude Code, and Grok Code use the shared bounded context-preamble helper. Remaining: extend same helper to custom socket engines once implemented.

items.title: Define universal core tools for swappable engines
items.summary: Separate universal tools like conversation read, memory read/write-propose, artifact refs, and permission requests from native-only workflow tools, with Gateway enforcement and receipts.
items.progress_note: In progress: added universal core-tool contract, Gateway grant builder, adapter prompt section, context-pack grant attachment, and conformance checks. Remaining: implement actual Gateway execution/read routes for conversation.read, memory.read, memory.write_propose, artifact.read, artifact.create_propose, and permission.request after proposal normalization.

items.title: Prove context continuity while switching engines
items.summary: Add live/context-continuity evals that establish conversation facts, switch among native, Codex, Claude Code, and Grok Code, and verify the new engine can code or reason using prior conversation and unified memory.
items.progress_note: In progress: added deterministic no-provider context continuity eval across native, Codex, Claude Code, and Grok Code engine IDs. Remaining: add opt-in live provider continuity eval when engines are locally available.

items.title: Retire legacy Gateway adapter host and shims
items.summary: Re-root phase is complete: Gateway route, status, startup, lifecycle, request-boundary, and Agent Runtime assembly logic now lives under gateway/**. Remaining work is retiring the thin legacy dashboard host and compatibility adapter shims before the allowed window closes.
items.progress_note: Retired the remaining unused Shell Socket adapter compatibility shims after live imports were confirmed to use canonical gateway/runtime/sockets/shell_socket/** modules. Remaining debt is the thin legacy dashboard host, agent_ws_bridge client-loader shim, and Agent Runtime compatibility shims.

items.title: Make the Agent Runtime Gateway socket live
items.summary: Graduate /ws/agent-runtime from contracted_not_live to a live Gateway socket so dashboard, CLI, SDK, and future shells submit turns through the same UI-agnostic boundary instead of adapter-hosted HTTP shims.

items.title: Migrate external engines beyond prompt-text context hydration
items.summary: Move external engines from prompt_text_compat toward structured_json or native session bridges where available, preserving the same AgentRuntimeTurnEnvelope while reducing token waste, ambiguity, duplicate transcript rows, and prompt-layer drift.

items.title: Add live useful-work evals for every selectable runtime
items.summary: Create live evals that ask each selectable runtime to perform practical agent work through InfRing, such as creating a small app, editing a file, reading prior context, using approved tools, and reporting receipts, then score whether it actually worked.

items.title: Make InfRing Native obey the same runtime abstraction as external engines
items.summary: Route InfRing Native through the same engine_id, context envelope, available_models, activity event, permission request, artifact ref, and receipt surfaces used by external engines so native orchestration is swappable rather than special-cased.

items.title: Make external runtime effects receipt-first
items.summary: Ensure every external runtime effect that matters has a durable InfRing receipt, including selected engine/model, context pack ref, approval decision, tool proposal, accepted artifact change, command outcome, final response, and failure classification.

items.title: Normalize external runtime activity into useful collapsible traces
items.summary: Capture and normalize framework activity streams into concise user-facing traces with real status text, tool calls, file changes, command results, failure events, and post-turn decision dialog, while keeping raw evidence behind refs and payload budgets.

items.title: Create an engine parity and usefulness scorecard
items.summary: Track each runtime engine against the same capabilities: discovery, model catalog, context continuity, useful work, approval pausing, universal tools, durable receipts, activity traces, error injection, and reload persistence.

items.title: Inject hard runtime failures into chat as first-class messages
items.summary: When an external framework fails from auth, quota, subscription, missing binary, timeout, payload budget, or transport failure, Gateway should emit a bounded chat-visible failure message plus trace refs and next actions instead of silently ending the turn.

items.title: Pause and resume external runtime turns through approval-gated tool calls
items.summary: External frameworks must not end a turn when a write/tool action needs permission. Gateway should hold the turn, emit a permission request, resume or deny based on the gate decision, and preserve receipts regardless of engine.
items.progress_note: Approval pause/resume gate is now wired through the existing npm/tooling gate name to the public Gateway route lifecycle guard, so governance runs the same turn-route -> permission_required -> approval-decision -> artifact-effect -> receipt proof.

items.title: Make framework context and persistence identical for native and external engines
items.summary: All engines, including InfRing native, Codex, Claude Code, Grok Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes, should receive the same bounded context pack, save turns through the same backend persistence path, and reload conversation state consistently.
items.progress_note: Public Gateway turn-route transcript persistence guard now proves route submission -> Gateway transcript overlay -> bounded budget -> context preview reload across six engines, and the runtime no longer duplicates user rows in raw transcript persistence after dispatch.

items.title: Project external runtime activity into clean semantic thinking/status traces
items.summary: Normalize Codex, Claude Code, Grok Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, and native runtime activity into concise user-facing status rows without raw JSON noise, duplicate rows, or forced started/finished/done sandwich text.
items.progress_note: Gateway activity projection now covers Codex-, Claude-, Grok-, OpenClaw-, and Hermes-shaped raw provider event fixtures, including nested input/args/tool fields, so chat-facing trace rows stay semantic without Shell cognition.

items.title: Implement real per-framework model discovery and selection
items.summary: The model menu should ask the active runtime for its available models when the framework owns model selection, otherwise fall back to InfRing provider discovery. Placeholder labels like default must not appear as models.
items.progress_note: Gateway model projection now exposes empty-catalog reasons and has a guard proving framework-native rows for Codex/Claude/Grok, inherited InfRing model policy for native/OpenClaw/Hermes, and no fake `default` model rows.

items.title: Retire remaining Gateway adapter compatibility shims
items.summary: Finish retiring declared Gateway compatibility shims under adapters/** after callers move to canonical gateway/** modules, while keeping adapter code translator-only.
items.progress_note: Shell Socket shims were retired; remaining debt includes the thin legacy dashboard host, agent_ws_bridge client-loader shim, and Agent Runtime compatibility shims.

items.title: Make the legacy dashboard replaceable without losing framework-router behavior
items.summary: Framework routing, permissions, context, persistence, model discovery, and status traces must live behind Gateway sockets so a rebuilt Shell or CLI can use the same behavior without copying dashboard cognition.
items.progress_note: This is the architectural safety check that the UI remains a face/lens, not the framework-router brain.

items.title: Graduate external engine transport from prompt-text compatibility toward structured transport
items.summary: Keep prompt-text context hydration as compatibility only, then move capable engines toward structured JSON context, refs, receipts, tool proposals, and eventually lower-token native context transfer.
items.progress_note: Added public Gateway route matrix guard proving every selected runtime engine receives AgentRuntimeStructuredTurn, context_pack.structured_transport refs match, prompt-text compatibility is explicitly transitional, and no model-provider secrets enter structured payloads.

items.title: Add cross-framework real-work replay proof for the coordinating face
items.summary: Create repeatable validation that runs small real tasks through at least native, Codex, Claude Code, and one open framework, proving context continuity, approval flow, persistence, status traces, and receipts.
items.progress_note: Added framework-coordination rollup guard command covering approval lifecycle, continuity, transcript persistence, activity projection, model projection, structured transport, and real-work replay proofs.
